instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Diversified holding company with operating businesses in industrial packaging, specialty chemicals, and food ingredients. Portfolio of 6 operating companies with combined revenues of €180M. Central corporate team of 25 managing strategy, M&A, and group finance. Evaluating cross-portfolio digital transformation and shared services platform implementation. We have a dedicated management team across core functions but operate with limited middle management layers. Budget cycles are annual with moderate flexibility for mid-year reallocation if a strong business case is presented. Innovation initiatives compete with day-to-day operational demands for team attention.
answers.pastInitiatives: Our engineering team adopted an agile methodology last year, moving from waterfall-style quarterly releases to 2-week sprints with continuous deployment. This reduced our release cycle time by 60% and improved cross-functional collaboration. However, adjacent teams (marketing, support) are still adapting to the faster cadence.
answers.strategicGoals: Customer retention has declined from 92% to 84% over the past 18 months, primarily among our mid-tier and enterprise segments. Exit interviews consistently cite product stagnation and poor digital self-service tools as reasons for leaving. We need to urgently modernize our customer-facing technology and proactively address the specific pain points driving churn before the trend becomes irreversible.
answers.teamSize: Our team includes 3 backend developers, 1 frontend developer, and 1 QA engineer, managed by the CTO who also acts as product owner. We outsource UI/UX design to a freelance designer as needed. The team can handle incremental product improvements but struggles to carve out focused time for larger innovation bets without compromising current sprint commitments.

input.changes_since_last: Product launch successful — 2 new features shipped. Customer NPS improved 20 points. Backlog of technical debt growing.

opportunities.title: Develop a Customer Digital Self-Service Platform to Curb Churn
opportunities.rationale: Customer retention is the most pressing strategic risk, driven by poor digital self-service tools. Modernizing this platform directly addresses exit interview findings and supports market defense goals. This initiative must be phased to manage technical debt while providing immediate value.

first_actions: Map out the core customer journey pain points (e.g., billing, support ticket submission) that currently drive churn.
Develop a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) scope focused solely on 2-3 critical self-service functions.
Allocate dedicated 'sprint capacity' for UI/UX redesign and frontend development, shielding it from operational feature creep.
resources_needed: Dedicated UX/UI budget (freelance or internal hire)
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in customer-reported pain points leading to a 10% lift in Net Promoter Score (NPS) within 12 months.
milestones: Completion of digital journey mapping and MVP scope (3 months)
Launch of initial self-service module (6 months)
Achieve quantifiable reduction in support tickets for covered functions (9 months)

opportunities.title: Institutionalize Agile Practices Across Non-Engineering Functions
opportunities.rationale: While the engineering team adopted agile successfully, adjacent teams (marketing, support) are struggling to adapt. To scale innovation beyond isolated sprints, standardized documentation and cross-functional training must be implemented. This addresses the 'culture' barrier and strengthens operational capability.

first_actions: Establish a formal Process Governance Working Group involving middle management representatives from all 6 operating companies.
Develop mandatory, standardized training modules for Agile principles (e.g., backlog grooming, user story writing) tailored for non-technical staff.
Designate 'Process Champions' within each adjacent team to drive adoption and accountability.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in time spent defining scope or requirements for cross-functional projects by 25% (measured via project intake forms).
milestones: Working group established and charter defined (2 months)
First cohort of non-technical staff completes training (4 months)
Standardized process adopted for at least two major cross-functional initiatives (8 months)

next_steps.action: Execute a comprehensive customer journey mapping exercise focused on identifying the top 3 points of friction in the digital self-service experience.
Mandate and dedicate a minimum of 20% of engineering sprint capacity specifically to addressing critical, customer-facing technical debt items identified during the mapping.
Formalize and initiate the Process Governance Working Group to select and train initial 'Process Champions' in marketing and support departments.

key_weaknesses: High customer churn risk due to poor digital self-service tools (Market Defense priority).
Structural limitations in middle management leading to difficulty scaling processes across portfolio companies.
Accumulating technical debt impeding the rapid development of user-facing features.

improvements: Successful product enhancements and launch of 2 new features contributing to a perceived uplift (NPS improved 20 points).
Formal adoption of Agile methodology in engineering, resulting in a significant 60% reduction in release cycle time.
Improved cross-functional collaboration within core technical teams.
persistent_gaps: The root cause of customer churn (digital self-service gaps) remains unaddressed at scale.
Organizational processes and culture lag behind technology adoption, particularly in non-technical departments.
Technical debt is growing, putting long-term stability at risk despite short-term feature wins.
achieved_milestones: Agile sprint deployment successfully implemented by the core engineering team.
Product launch demonstrating capability to handle complex features and rapid iteration.

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: The focus has shifted from general process implementation (Agile adoption) to urgent business-critical needs: customer retention and digital modernization. While operational improvements are visible, the underlying structural weaknesses in digital experience and organizational scaling remain highly critical.
